Asquith, W.H., and Thompson, D.B., 2008, Alternative regression equations for estimation of annual peak-streamflow frequency for undeveloped watersheds in Texas using PRESS minimization: U.S. Geological Survey Scientific Investigations Report 2008-5084, 40 p.

notes: SUPERSEDED IN PRACTICE: SIR 2008-5084 (Table 8, region Statewide) is followed by Asquith and Roussel, 2009, SIR 2009-5087, whose authors prefer its OmegaEM equations; NSS's peak-flow snapshot does not serve that report, nor the 96 equations of Asquith and Slade, 1997, WRI 96-4307, so neither is stored. What NSS serves is kept. CITATIONS NSS GETS WRONG: NSS cites WRI 98-4015 for GC1489, but that report excludes urban basins and has no impervious-cover equation; the set is Veenhuis and Gannett, WRI 86-4069, Table 8. NSS cites WRI 98-4178 for GC1493, but the set is WRI 98-4015's large-basin equations. Seven reports, then: 98-4015 (2 regions), 98-4178 (3), 86-4069, 82-18, 96-4072, 80-17 and 2008-5084 (1 each). All are kept because each is the only set for its area or land use; the regional sets and the Statewide set overlap; region_preference puts the regional sets first and Statewide elsewhere (an owner's decision of 2026-11-08), and the Colorado sets split at 32 mi2 by region_limits. region= overrides. INTERVALS: 98-4015 and 98-4178 give the prediction variance as s^2(1 + h0), with h0 = x'[X'WX]^-1 x from an unscaled matrix. flowfreq computes model_error_variance + x'Ux, so model_error_variance = s^2 and covariance = s^2 times the printed matrix, reordered to intercept first (98-4015 prints Area, Slope, Constant). SIR 2008-5084 is the same; its matrices are printed only in Appendix 2's R output, as tmp in finalQt, in the order constant, A^lambda, log10 P, and s times the root of their diagonal gives the printed Std. Error columns. No covariance is printed for 86-4069, 82-18, 96-4072 or 80-17, so intervals use sep_log. 86-4069 prints an average standard error of prediction; 82-18, 96-4072 and 80-17 print only a standard error of estimate, stored as sep_log because it is the only error they give. It omits coefficient sampling error, so those intervals are narrower than a true SEP. 96-4072's 0.036 log10^2 mean square error for its 100-year equation agrees with its 46 percent (0.1887^2). REPORT ERRORS: (1) 98-4178 Table 3's region 3 matrix is not the matrix of region 3's printed equation. It equals, to all five printed decimals, the constant and CDA block of a three-term fit that also has stream slope, with 08065800 Bedias Creek (region 2 in Table 1) in region 3. The two-term fit gives 0.16508, -0.06928, 0.03398 and reproduces Table 2's region 3 equations. The report's example uses the printed matrix (h0 = 0.29634, where the two-term matrix gives 0.0605), so it is stored as printed and region 3 intervals are wider than the fit supports. (2) 98-4178 Table 1 counts 80 stations in region 2 and 41 in region 3 after the exclusions the text lists; Table 2 says 79 and 42, and refits agree with Table 2 once Bedias Creek moves. (3) 98-4178 p. 19 gives the upper limit as 9,670 in the computation and 9,760 in the sentence after it; 9,670 is right. (4) 98-4015 p. I-1 prints a large-basin weight of 0.070 where the computation uses 0.70. (5) 2008-5084 Table 8 prints s = 0.3548 and adjusted R2 0.7458 for Q100; Appendix 2 prints 0.3545 and 0.7461, and 0.12386 / sqrt(0.12205) = 0.3545, so 0.3545 is stored. (6) 82-18's effects table (p. 53) uses urbanization indexes 36 and 9, the index's limits. Fifteen of its 16 flows reproduce to 0.34 percent; Turtle Creek's 5-year minimum prints 1,960 where the equation gives 1,942 (0.9 percent), and that cell is pinned. NOT STORED, BECAUSE NO FIELD OR NO SEPARATE REGION FITS: 98-4015's equation 3 weights the two Colorado sets by log10 A from 10 to 100 mi2 (the example reproduces in the test, outside the small set's calibrated range), and its equations 4 and 5 weight their limits. 80-17 caps K at KMAX from its figure 2. Shape-factor limits apply to 98-4015 (0.30-3.93, 3.79-18.43) and 96-4072 (1.0-15), and 98-4178 lists others on p. 12; these are in no NSS parameter set, so they are left here rather than as applicability limits that would refuse every StreamStats basin. 96-4072 limits its equations to about 45 mi of Marble Falls. Also not stored: SIR 2008-5084's other five equation sets (Tables 4-7, 9), which NSS does not serve, and each report's R2. Limits are the ones each report recommends where it gives both: 86-4069 uses 2.0-20 mi2 (data 2.31-51.3), 82-18 uses 3-40 mi2 and 12-33 (data 1.25-66.4, 10-36). CHECKS: 80-17's Table 10 per-gage estimates (22 gages, 132 values) reproduce to its rounding from Table 5. 98-4015 and 98-4178 refit from their Table 1 gage data. No report prints per-gage regression estimates except 80-17. 96-4072 has no worked example, no matrix and no per-gage estimates, so its check is NSS and the MSE alone. NSS DIFFERENCES: none in any AEP, flow, coefficient or limit, only the two citations above and NSS's form for URBAN and IMPERV, (100 + x), which folds the 100 into the constant and gives the same flow.
